item.title: Fed’s Goolsbee Wants to See More Evidence of Cooling Inflation
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said he’s encouraged by a recent cooling in inflation but wants to see more of the same in coming months to be sure it’s falling back to the central bank’s 2% target.

item.title: Canada Must Remove Retaliation to Avoid New Tariffs, Greer Says
item.description: Canada needs to scrap its retaliatory trade measures against US products to avoid new tariffs from the White House that are set to take effect next week, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said.

item.title: ‘Monkey Island’ Creator Finds Wealthy Investor for ‘Thimbleweed Park 2’
item.description: Ron Gilbert didn’t want to go with a traditional publisher for ‘Thimbleweed Park 2,’ so he took an unorthodox route

item.title: Election Angst Fuels Bruising Week in Brazil Markets
item.description: Brazilian assets posted some of the biggest losses in the world this week amid growing angst over the October presidential election.

item.title: Trump Family-Tied Dronemakers (UMAC, PUSA) Get a Boost From New US Tariffs
item.description: Drone makers and suppliers, including two companies with ties to the Trump family, rallied Friday after the White House said it’s applying a tariff on imports of unmanned aircraft systems and their components.

item.title: Bonds Become ‘Really Difficult to Trade’ as Correlations Unwind
item.description: Bond traders face a welter of confusion as fixed-income markets respond more to geopolitical risk and inflation rather than taking cues from traditional signals like US economic growth, according to AlphaSimplex Group’s Kathryn Kaminski.

item.title: GTC Investor May Sell Stake to Break With Hungary Central Bank
item.description: Optima Befektetési Zrt. is considering selling its controlling stake in Globe Trade Centre SA, a move that would end the controversial influence of Hungary’s central bank over one of eastern Europe’s biggest property developers.

item.title: Kushner’s Thrive Capital Invests $215 Million in Amazon
item.description: Joshua Kushner’s Thrive Capital has bought up roughly $215 million worth of shares in Amazon.com Inc., building on the venture firm’s push to invest in public companies.

item.title: Picky Investors Push Back on High-Grade Prices After Debt Deluge
item.description: Blue-chip firms are swarming the US debt market to finance everything from acquisitions to the artificial intelligence buildout. But investors are getting pickier about what they’ll buy, and at what price, as the borrowing frenzy takes its toll.

item.title: Carlyle, CVC Team Up to Bid for Security Systems Group Bauwatch
item.description: Carlyle Group Inc. and CVC Capital Partners Plc are exploring a joint takeover of security systems provider Bauwatch, people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: Airbus Finds System Faults on Air India Jet During Mid-Air Drop
item.description: Airbus SE discovered hydraulic system faults on an Air India Ltd. jet that dropped about 300 feet in mid-flight last week, according to a preliminary assessment by the planemaker.

item.title: Bessent Asked to Justify Yen Intervention in Letter from Warren
item.description: Senator Elizabeth Warren pressed Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to explain the Trump administration’s justification for intervening in the yen, extending the senior Democrat’s pattern of scrutinizing the Trump administration’s foreign-exchange policies.

item.title: UK Starts Process to Ease EV Mandate in Boon for Carmakers
item.description: The UK will look at watering down its zero-emission vehicle sales mandate, a win for automakers that have been pushing new Prime Minister Andy Burnham to bring forward a review of the targets.

item.title: Colombia Bond Market Perks Up After De la Espriella’s Election
item.description: Colombia’s local corporate bond sales are rebounding after four years in the doldrums as the election of a market-friendly government stokes investor demand for local assets and triggers a drop in sovereign yields.

item.title: Kenya Eyes Eurobond, Debt Swaps in $5.4 Billion Financing Plan
item.description: Kenya plans to raise $815 million in a eurobond sale by the end of December to finance its budget deficit and reduce debt costs, according to the National Treasury.

item.title: Treasuries Rise as Weak Retail Sales Dampen Fed Rate-Hike Expectations
item.description: Short-dated Treasuries rose after weak July retail sales data further eroded expectations for Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes in the coming months, which were already crumbling based on employment and inflation data.

item.title: Dollar Slides to May Low as Weak Retail Sales Dim Rate Bets
item.description: The dollar fell to the lowest since May after an unexpectedly weak reading of US retail sales pushed traders to further pare back their expectations for an interest-rate hike this year.

item.title: French Top Court Blocks Macron Social Media Ban for Young Teens
item.description: France’s highest court blocked a ban on social media for children under 15 that was approved in Parliament last month, in a setback for President Emmanuel Macron who championed the bill.

item.title: SpaceX Completes Its $60 Billion Cursor Acquisition
item.description: SpaceX has completed a $60 billion acquisition of artificial intelligence coding startup Cursor, a key part of Elon Musk’s bid to gain ground on rivals Anthropic PBC and OpenAI.

item.title: EdgeConneX Seeks $2.5 Billion Bank Pledge for Data Center Power
item.description: EQT-backed EdgeConneX Inc. is asking banks to guarantee as much as $2.5 billion in power costs, joining a wave of data center builders turning to new financing playbooks to fuel growth.

item.title: Radiant World Said to Sell Aluminum Stockpile to STG Group
item.description: Metals trader Radiant World agreed to sell a stockpile of aluminum to STG Group, according to people familiar with the matter, in a move that will bring in liquidity to the firm.

item.title: India Raises $50 Billion of Diaspora Dollars, Ends Swap Facility
item.description: India mobilized more than $50 billion from its drive to attract overseas capital since June, giving the country’s central bank a bigger headroom to bolster foreign exchange reserves and support the weak rupee.

item.title: US Retail Sales Fall Most Since May 2025 After Solid Demand Run
item.description: US retail sales fell in July by the most in more than a year as consumers pulled back on purchases at online stores and auto dealers.

item.title: White Sugar Rally Boosts Refining as Supply Outlook Tightens
item.description: White sugar futures in London headed for a third straight weekly gain, boosting refining margins as concerns over tightening supplies stay in focus.

item.title: US Stock Futures Up as Strong Earnings, Benign Data Drive Gains
item.description: US equities are poised to end the week at all-time highs, extending a momentum driven by robust earnings and cooler inflation readings.

item.title: US Oil Growth Faces Headwinds as Shale Producers Cut Spending
item.description: Some of the largest US oil companies are dialing back capital spending in the country’s shale basins as they use the windfall from high crude prices to boost shareholder returns and pay down debt rather than accelerate production growth.

item.title: Hunt for AI-Proof Trades Turns Convenience Shops Into Hot Stocks
item.description: Convenience store stocks are having their moment, riding a wave of investor demand for more defensive plays as angst over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence boom and the ongoing conflict in Iran drive increased market turbulence.

item.title: ‘FOMO Insurance’ Drives Options Buying Spree as Stocks Rally On
item.description: As the stock market keeps surging to record highs, a growing worry among investors isn’t that it may come tumbling back down. It’s fear of missing out.

item.title: Indonesia’s 2027 Budget Positions Miners, EV Makers as Winners
item.description: Miners, electric vehicle manufacturers, and battery producers are set to win big under Indonesia’s state budget next year, analysts said. The gains will be driven by President Prabowo Subianto’s push to boost the commodity sector and slash reliance on costly imported fossil fuels.

item.title: Airtel Mulls UK Listing of its Money Unit in Dollars
item.description: Airtel Africa Plc is considering having its mobile payments arm trade in US dollars when it lists it in London later this year, an arrangement that’s only been seen a handful of times.
